Subject: Proposed redlines: derivative output carveout, telemetry retention, training opt-out (MSA + Order Form)

Hannah —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Attached is our redline to the MSA and a short order-form addendum that our GC asked me to surface. High-level asks are below: please confirm Redwood's position and whether you can accept the order-form opt-out mechanics (we need a clear checkbox/line-item in the OF).

Key commercial/legal asks:
- Customer requests assignment of "Derivative Output" where productization is planned (we propose assignment of Output for specific Productization Projects listed in the OF).
- If assignment is not acceptable, customer wants an exclusive productization license for a 12-month window post-delivery.
- Training/data use: customer requires an explicit opt-in for Redwood to include customer data/outputs in model training. Default should be opt-out unless otherwise stated.
- Telemetry & logs: retention capped at 90 days for event-level telemetry tied to customer identifiers; aggregated telemetry allowed for service improvement.
- Feedback license: customer will provide feedback; requests that feedback be used only in anonymized, aggregated form unless they opt-in.

Can you review and circulate internal counter-language by EOD Friday? Also flag any commercial delta so we can prep procurement.

Attached: MedLink_MSA_redline_v1.pdf, MedLink_OrderForm_requested_clauses.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 3 May 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed redlines: derivative output carveout, telemetry retention, training opt-out (MSA + Order Form)

Hannah / Ben —

I've reviewed the redline. Below are concise legal options and suggested language fragments we can use in the MSA/Order Form. My preference is to avoid broad assignment unless it's narrowly scoped.

Option 1 — Preferred (License with productization carveout):
- Clause language (suggested): "Customer retains title to Customer Data and Output. Subject to Customer's election in the Order Form, Customer may grant Redwood a time-limited, exclusive, transferable license to use specific Outputs for Productization Projects listed in the Order Form for a period not to exceed twelve (12) months following delivery. Such license shall be limited to the Productization Projects expressly identified and shall terminate automatically upon completion of the listed projects."

Option 2 — Assignment (limited):
- If MedLink insists on assignment, require:
  - Narrowly enumerated deliverables + project list in the OF
  - One-time assignment fee + milestone payments
  - Redwood retains right to use de-identified, aggregated Output for service improvement unless Customer affirmatively opts out in the Order Form.

Training / Data Use (redline suggestion):
- "Redwood will not use Customer Data or Output to train or improve models used to provide Services to other customers except where Customer has explicitly opted in via the Order Form. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use de-identified and aggregated telemetry for general service improvements provided such telemetry does not include Customer Confidential Information or PII."

Telemetry retention (operational suggestion):
- Event-level telemetry tied to identifiers: 90 days max.
- Aggregated metrics and anonymized performance telemetry: retained up to 24 months.

Feedback license (language):
- "Customer grants Redwood a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free right to use Feedback provided by Customer, solely for the purpose of improving the Services, provided that such Feedback is anonymized and does not include Customer Confidential Information."

I attached a short snippet file (proposed_training_optout_clause.txt) with redlined text. If Ben can confirm commercial tradeoffs, I'll prepare a redline to return to MedLink showing Option 1 + a fallback assignment path at a commercial premium.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Quick commercial readout — Hannah / Laura:

Assignment vs License:

If they insist on assignment, propose: 12-month exclusive assignment for numbered projects only, plus a 20% uplift on the first-year committed spend and a $50k one-time productization validation fee.

Training opt-out:
- Accept opt-out via order form (checkbox). If they opt-out, apply a 10% surcharge on usage rates to cover model improvement impact and potential loss of reuse economies.

Telemetry retention:
- Agree to 90 days for event-level telemetry tied to identifiers; propose 180 days for logs used for safety/compliance with stricter access controls. (If legal insists on 90 days, we can accept but need operational confirmation).
